antipatterns.title: Claimed a fork as my own work
antipatterns.mistake: A forked repository slipped into the portfolio as a personal project.
antipatterns.whyBad: A portfolio's core promise is that every claim is the owner's own work. A fork is someone else's — and an AI agent or recruiter would trust a false claim as fact.
antipatterns.fix: Filter the fork flag everywhere: live GitHub fetch, the hourly metrics snapshot, and the portfolio data itself.
antipatterns.lesson: Verify ownership before claiming credit — never trust the shape of a data source over its content.

antipatterns.title: Hardcoded dark-theme colors broke the light theme
antipatterns.mistake: Components used literal dark-theme colors, so switching the theme produced white text on white background.
antipatterns.whyBad: A theme is a cross-cutting concern — local color literals silently violate the global invariant, and only a full visual pass catches it.
antipatterns.fix: Semantic tokens through CSS variables (ink/paper/muted/faint/accent) with a dark variant; no raw palette colors in components.
antipatterns.lesson: Design tokens are invariants, not styling sugar. If the invariant is global, the enforcement must be too.

antipatterns.title: Passed raw JSON Schema to an SDK that wanted zod
antipatterns.mistake: registerTool accepted the config but every request 500'd — the SDK v2 expects a zod schema, not a raw JSON Schema object.
antipatterns.whyBad: A misleading API surface silently accepts input it can't use; the failure appeared only at request time, not at registration.
antipatterns.fix: Convert with z.fromJSONSchema() and verify with an integration test (tools/list + tools/call) before shipping.
antipatterns.lesson: Verify the SDK's expected input format with a real call — compile-time acceptance is not runtime acceptance.

antipatterns.title: A live data source broke and nothing noticed
antipatterns.mistake: get_articles started returning 403 from dev.to in production; the tool gracefully fell back to an error and stayed silent.
antipatterns.whyBad: Graceful degradation without monitoring turns an outage into a quiet lie: the tool answered, but with no data.
antipatterns.fix: Add a User-Agent header + committed-snapshot fallback, and a CI smoke step that calls the real tool, not just tools/list.
antipatterns.lesson: A smoke test that lists tools proves discovery, not function. Exercise the real call path.

antipatterns.title: Asserted against the wrong wire format
antipatterns.mistake: A CI grep looked for "count" in a response where the field is JSON-escaped inside an SSE text payload (\"count\") — the check never matched.
antipatterns.whyBad: An assertion against an imagined format is worse than none: it passed when it should have failed loudly.
antipatterns.fix: Match the bare token and document why; re-check the real byte-level output when writing assertions.
antipatterns.lesson: Before asserting on output, look at the output. Tests encode assumptions — make the assumptions explicit.

antipatterns.title: Fire-and-forget work silently vanished in production
antipatterns.mistake: An unawaited promise (void task) was expected to run after the response — the runtime cancelled it, and the KV counter never wrote.
antipatterns.whyBad: Local tests in Node don't cancel pending promises, so the code was green while production silently lost the work.
antipatterns.fix: Run background work inside ctx.waitUntil() in Workers; keep a void fallback only where the runtime doesn't cancel.
antipatterns.lesson: Runtime lifecycles differ between dev and prod. If work outlives the request, it must be registered with the runtime.

antipatterns.title: Assumed a platform feature was enforced
antipatterns.mistake: A Cloudflare rate-limit binding deployed cleanly, but limit() returned success on every call — enforcement simply wasn't active on the plan.
antipatterns.whyBad: A binding that deploys is not a binding that enforces; without an empirical burst test the protection was imaginary.
antipatterns.fix: Test the guard with a deliberately low limit before trusting it; document plan-dependent behavior explicitly.
antipatterns.lesson: Verify platform behavior empirically — configuration acceptance and runtime enforcement are different contracts.
